A B-tree index is a data structure that contains a set of keys and pointers. The keys are the values of the indexed column, and the pointers point to the next level of the index or to the rows in the table. The lowest level of the index is called the leaf level, which contains the pointers to the rows in the table.

To search for a value in a B-tree index, the database uses a specific algorithm. It starts at the root level

    entry. When an entry's TTL expires, it is considered invalid and will be removed

    entry is evicted.

            that don't specify a TTL. None means no expiration.
